key_insight: A classical two-point finite volume method loses its nominal second-order accuracy when the heat equation includes a measure-valued source, with convergence limited by spatial dimension.
engineering_relevance: For simulations with point loads or other singular sources, engineers should expect reduced mesh-convergence rates and choose discretizations accordingly.
method: Analyze finite volume convergence for a time-dependent diffusion-reaction/heat equation with measure-valued forcing
Extend prior finite-element theory to the classical two-point flux finite volume scheme
Compare theoretical convergence limits in 2D and 3D with computational tests using a Dirac delta source
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational tests with a Dirac delta point source that match the predicted reduced convergence rates: order 1 in two dimensions and 0.5 in three dimensions.
watch_item: The main limitation is that singular or measure-valued sources can sharply reduce accuracy, so standard refinement may not recover second-order behavior.
paper_title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
